name: Verified Claims Are Fidelity-Checked
description: Every verification of a model TRANSLATED FROM CODE should be backed by a passed model↔code fidelity check — a verdict is fully code-grounded only when the model provably reproduces the real code. Vacuous for spec-first / authored IML (no source to conform to).
rationale: A proof holds of the MODEL. When the model was translated from real code, a fidelity (conformance) check is what links the two — without it a 'verified' verdict is only provisional and may not reflect the deployed system. The requirement is guarded by `F SourceCode` so it applies only when there IS source to conform to: a spec-first / authored-IML session (no SourceCode artifact) passes vacuously, since the IML itself is the artifact, not a translation. Fidelity is optional in the current flow, so a missing check on code-derived models is a flagged gap, not a hard failure (hence warning).

examples.passes: Verify(model) → ConformanceResult(passed) linking the model to the real code
examples.fails: Verify(model) with no passed fidelity/conformance check
